name: Myron Wentz
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, USANA Health Sciences; founder, Sanoviv Medical Institute (Rosarito, Mexico)
profile: Microbiologist (PhD, University of Utah) born 1940 in Napoleon, North Dakota. Founded Gull Laboratories (diagnostic tests) in 1974, then USANA Health Sciences in 1992, a NYSE-listed nutritional supplements/skincare MLM in which he still holds roughly 40%. Retired as USANA chairman in Dec 2019; spends most of his time at Sanoviv, the holistic medical centre he founded in 1998. Still gave a keynote at USANA Live 2025.
interesting_fact: He enjoys snorkeling and watching coral reef videos on YouTube; he renounced US citizenship in the mid-1990s and claims St. Kitts & Nevis citizenship.
deep_cut_fact: He started Gull Laboratories in 1974 as a one-person operation that developed a diagnostic test for Epstein-Barr virus; later gave $10M to his alma mater North Central College (Naperville, IL), helping fund the Wentz Concert Hall, and its science center bears his name.
notes: Lives mostly in Rosarito, Mexico (Sanoviv). Best route is via USANA corporate communications. Health/longevity angle (cellular nutrition) is his signature theme.

name: Weijian Shan
current_role: Executive Chairman and Co-Founder, PAG (Asia-focused alternative investment firm); independent director, Alibaba Group
profile: Beijing-born (1954) private equity investor who spent six years as a sent-down youth in the Gobi Desert before studying in the US (MBA USF, PhD UC Berkeley). After the World Bank, Wharton faculty and J.P. Morgan, he was TPG/Newbridge's top Asia dealmaker (incl. Korea First Bank), then built PAG from 2010 into a ~$50B+ AUM Asia alternatives firm. Author of three books; British Museum trustee.
interesting_fact: His 2019 memoir 'Out of the Gobi: My Story of China and America' recounts laboring in the Gobi during the Cultural Revolution; Janet Yellen was one of his Berkeley thesis advisors.
deep_cut_fact: Before Wall Street he was an assistant professor at the Wharton School for six years, where he founded the academic journal China Economic Review; he first came to Beijing's Institute of Foreign Trade in 1975 to study English.
notes: Very public: frequent op-ed writer (FT, NYT, Foreign Affairs) and conference speaker; books (Money Games, Money Machine) give a natural hook. ir@pag.com is investor-only; info@pag.com (Hong Kong HQ) is the general route.

name: Rosana Camargo De Arruda Botelho
current_role: Controlling shareholder (via family holdings incl. Participações Morro Vermelho) of Mover Participações, formerly Grupo Camargo Corrêa
profile: One of the three daughters of Sebastião Camargo, who founded Camargo Corrêa in Jaú, São Paulo in 1939. She and her sisters Renata and Regina inherited control after their mother Dirce died in 2013; the group, renamed Mover, is run by non-family professionals. Mover has been selling assets in 2025-26 (e.g. its Motiva stake to Bradesco BBI) to cut debt. Widow/partner of businessman-aviator Fernando de Arruda Botelho; about 76.
interesting_fact: The family's controlling holding, Morro Vermelho, is named after a farm in Jaú, Sebastião Camargo's hometown, and also gave its name to the group's executive aviation arm, Morro Vermelho Táxi Aéreo.
notes: Very private; no personal public channels. Her daughter Daniela Camargo Botelho de Abreu Pereira is the only family member on Mover's board (since 2024). Best route is Mover Participações corporate communications (moverpar.com.br, blocked to automated fetch). Name sometimes spelled 'Rossana'.

name: Qiu Guogen
current_role: Founder, executive managing partner and chief investment officer, Shanghai Chongyang Investment (重阳投资)
profile: Zhejiang-born veteran of China's private securities fund industry. After an economics master's at Renmin University and a stint (1993-95) at an investment arm of the former Junan Securities, he began investing professionally in 1996 and founded Chongyang Investment in Shanghai in 2001, long one of China's largest private equity-securities funds. Ranks on Hurun lists jointly with wife Luo Yi (approx. RMB 7.5B in 2026).
interesting_fact: Chongyang was described around 2010 as China's largest private securities investment firm; its style is value investing aimed at 'all-weather' returns across market cycles.
deep_cut_fact: At a 2015 Hangzhou wealth-management forum he recalled that after university he interned for three months at the Zhejiang provincial branch of China Construction Bank in Hangzhou, and argued that 'risk and return are matched' (风险和收益是匹配的).
notes: Low-profile; rarely gives interviews. Route would be via Chongyang Investment's official website/office in Shanghai (no published press email found). Wealth shared with wife Luo Yi.

name: Yang Ying
current_role: Largest shareholder (~34%) and co-controller of Xiamen Amoytop Biotech (特宝生物, SSE STAR 688278)
profile: Investor in Xiamen Amoytop Biotech, a Xiamen-based maker of recombinant protein and long-acting modified drugs (e.g. Pegbing peginterferon for hepatitis B, Yipeisheng). Forbes lists her as a director and says her husband Lan Chun was chairman; Sun Li is now chairman/GM. She holds about 33.9% (2025 Q1 report); Amoytop's 2025 revenue grew ~31% to RMB 3.7B with net profit ~RMB 1.04B.
interesting_fact: Amoytop, founded in the mid-1990s, has never seen its controlling holders (Yang Ying, Sun Li and concert party) sell a share since its 2020 STAR Market IPO, and they pledged not to reduce holdings for five years.
notes: Extremely low profile; no personal bio found online and she is not alive-confirmed by any recent personal news (still listed as top shareholder in 2025 filings). Common name - many unrelated academics named Yang Ying. Approach via Amoytop's company office/board secretary.

name: Ricardo Cisneros
current_role: Head of the Ricardo Cisneros branch of the Cisneros family business (Cisneros Corporation, Coral Gables, FL), now run largely by his sons
profile: Son of Diego Cisneros, founder of Venezuela's Cisneros group (Pepsi bottling, Venevisión). He and brother Gustavo ran the group from 1970 and jointly appeared on Forbes' 1996 billionaires list; the brothers formally split the holding in 2008. His branch's interests include Cervecería Regional, the Leones del Caracas baseball club, industrial investments and private equity.
interesting_fact: In 1992 the Cisneros brothers were part of the consortium that bought Univision, the leading US Spanish-language TV network, for US$550 million.
deep_cut_fact: In July 2024 he signed a joint venture with PDVSA to revive oil fields in Venezuela's western Zulia state, targeting a quadrupling of output to about 50,000 barrels a day by 2026 - an energy angle for the podcast.
notes: Not to be confused with brother Gustavo Cisneros (died Dec 2023). Full name Ricardo José Cisneros Rendiles. Very private; no published contacts found. Sons Eduardo, Andrés and Henrique lead the business day to day, so outreach likely via Cisneros Corporation in Coral Gables. Alive status not explicitly confirmed (active in 2024 deal).

name: Rupen Ashwin Choksi
current_role: Managing Director, Resins and Plastics Ltd. (Choksi-family company, Mumbai); member of the Asian Paints promoter group
profile: Son of the late Ashwin Choksi, former non-executive chairman of Asian Paints, and grandson of co-founder Chimanlal Choksi. His wealth derives from the Choksi family's promoter stake in Asian Paints, India's largest paint maker; he is not on the Asian Paints board but runs family industrial businesses including Resins and Plastics Ltd. (director since 2007) and is a director of Pragati Chemicals.
interesting_fact: His grandfather Chimanlal Choksi was one of the four friends who co-founded Asian Paints in 1942; the Choksi, Dani and Vakil families still share promoter control.
notes: Very low profile; no interviews or social accounts found. Company-registry sites list him as MD of Resins and Plastics Ltd. Route via Asian Paints investor/secretarial office is indirect since he is not an Asian Paints director.

name: Arno Schodl
current_role: Co-founder and CTO/Technical Director, think-cell Software GmbH (Berlin)
profile: German computer scientist (PhD in computer graphics, Georgia Tech) who worked at Microsoft Research and McKinsey before co-founding think-cell with Markus Hannebauer in 2002. think-cell's PowerPoint charting add-in became the de facto standard for consultants and bankers; PE firm Cinven bought a majority stake in 2021, and the founders retain a ~30% stake. He oversees R&D, QA and customer care.
interesting_fact: Before co-founding think-cell he worked at both Microsoft Research and McKinsey & Company; the company describes think-cell as 'the de facto standard' for professional PowerPoint presentations.
deep_cut_fact: As a Georgia Tech PhD student he was lead author of 'Video Textures' (SIGGRAPH 2000, with Richard Szeliski, David Salesin and Irfan Essa), a widely cited paper on synthesising endless, non-repeating video from a short clip. He is also a regular C++ conference speaker on think-cell's open-source ranges library.
notes: Engineer-founder, more visible in the C++ developer community (CppCast, NDC TechTown, Meeting C++) than in business press. A technical/C++ angle is likely to land well. Name also spelled Schoedl.
